cves.headline: MCP Atlassian before 0.22.0 lets search return items outside filters

name: Hardware Child Block Incorrectly Connected to Parent System
title: CWE-1276: Hardware Child Block Incorrectly Connected to Parent System
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in MCP servers, the connector layer that links AI assistants to outside tools. The one CVE here is in MCP Atlassian before 0.22.0, where a search can return items outside the filters that were set. The flaw sits in how the server wires its filter logic to the parent system, so the connection between the request and the data it should be allowed to reach is wrong. An attacker can then see records the filter was meant to hide, which means exposure of content the user never asked for and should not receive. The product named is MCP Atlassian.
description: Signals between a hardware IP and the parent system design are incorrectly connected causing security risks.

mitigations.description: System-level verification may be used to ensure that components are correctly connected and that design security requirements are not violated due to interactions between various IP blocks.

extended_description: Individual hardware IP must communicate with the parent system in order for the product to function correctly and as intended. If implemented incorrectly, while not causing any apparent functional issues, may cause security issues. For example, if the IP should only be reset by a system-wide hard reset, but instead the reset input is connected to a software-triggered debug mode reset (which is also asserted during a hard reset), integrity of data inside the IP can be violated.
